content.title: About
content.content: Berry strudel is a pastry made from thin rolled dough filled with fresh berries (commonly blueberries, strawberries or a mixed berry blend) and lightly sweetened. The dough is crisp, while the filling is juicy and aromatic. Strudel is often served warm, dusted with powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional Austrian strudel originated in Tyrol in the 19th century.
Berry versions became popular across Europe after frozen berries became widely available in the early 20th century.
The thin dough is made from flour, water, butter and a small amount of eggs, without yeast.
The original recipe used only apples, but berry variations are now considered classic.
Strudel is frequently served with vanilla sauce or ice cream.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Berries provide vitamin C, vitamin E and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the berries and whole‑grain dough promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The dough uses a modest amount of butter, keeping saturated fat levels relatively low.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs supply B1, B2 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Moderate sugar content
items.content: When prepared with controlled sweetening, the dessert can be a healthier treat.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Overly sweet strudel can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dough and butter make the pastry energy‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Eggs are commonly used in the dough; they should be substituted for those with an allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve strudel warm, sliced into portions. It can be dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with melted butter, or accompanied by vanilla sauce, ice cream, or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep strudel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven before serving to restore a crisp crust.
